section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Israel is called the "hosts of Hashem" because of their service of subjugation and transformation, drawing a parallel to a military army that conquers new territory and exhibits total self-nullification to the king.
section.t: And the maamar continues,
(after explaining at length that the drawing down of the principal Shechinah into the lower realms is through the service of subjugation [Itkafya] and transformation [Ithapcha]),
that for this reason Israel is called by the name "Hosts of Hashem",
due to their service of subjugation and transformation.
And one can explain this as follows:
The difference between an army
(men of valor)
and the ministers and the like who deal with improving the affairs of the state is in two matters.
First, regarding the effect on the state that is accomplished through them:
For by going out to war to conquer the enemy,
a novelty is created in the king's state,
in that even that land which was previously under the enemy's dominion becomes the king's state
(this is not the case with the improvement of the state and the strengthening of its power through the ministers, which is not in a manner of novelty).
Second, regarding the army itself:
their self-sacrifice and dedication to the king is beyond all limitations,
to the point that they risk their lives when they go out to war,
and beyond this, they are always prepared
(even not during wartime)
to give their lives without deviating from what they were commanded,
the quality of self-nullification.
And this is that Israel is called by the name "Hosts of Hashem" due to their service of subjugation and transformation,
for the matter of transformation,
that one transforms the world which appears to be a reality
[this is the matter of the falsehood of the world]
into a sanctuary and dwelling place for Him, blessed be He,
is analogous to the conquest that comes through war.
And from the virtues of transformation is the novelty.
For that darkness is turned into light is a novelty.
And the matter of subjugation is the war itself,
that one fights against his evil inclination,
and the virtue of subjugation is in the matter of self-nullification,
that one removes and sets himself aside for the sake of the will of the Holy One, blessed be He.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section draws a parallel to physical warfare, explaining that just as treasures are lavishly given to the army to win, so too is the supernal treasure given lavishly to the "hosts of Hashem" to ensure their victory.
section.t: And the maamar continues,
that just as in physical warfare,
in order to win the war, they expend the treasures and give them
(through the minister-officials)
to the men of the army so that they will win the war,
so too is it above,
that in order for the hosts of Hashem to win the war,
they are given,
and in a manner of lavish expenditure,
the supernal treasure.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section distinguishes between the two services of subjugation and transformation, explaining that the drawing down through subjugation is loftier, revealing the essential light of Ein Sof that transcends connection to worlds, and connects this to the concept of the passing of a tzaddik and the attainment of the Yechidah level after twenty years.
section.t: Now, the difference between the two services of subjugation and transformation is also in the drawing down that is drawn through them.
For the drawing down through the service of subjugation is loftier than the drawing down through the service of transformation.
For "when the sitra achra is subjugated
(specifically subjugation)
the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, is elevated throughout all worlds,"
the drawing down and revelation of the Essence of the Ein Sof, which is above any relation to the worlds,
therefore this drawing down is called "elevation" [istalkus],
because it is a revelation of the light that is in the aspect of transcendence.
[And it is noteworthy,
that so too is it regarding the passing of tzaddikim,
which is not a departure in its simple sense, Heaven forbid,
for the shepherds of Israel do not abandon their flock,
but rather, on the contrary,
it is a loftier drawing down,
a drawing down from the soul of the tzaddik itself, which is not limited within a vessel or garment,
and it is called "elevation" because it is a revelation that is above being clothed in vessels.
And particularly after twenty years,
when the matter of "selling the property of his father" is also added
[which also applies to the students of the tzaddik, who are called sons],
and it is explained in Likkutei Torah
that this that our sages said,
"and to sell the property of his father until he is twenty years old," is because then the encompassing lights of Abba enter him,
encompassing lights that are above being clothed in vessels.
And one can connect this also with the fact that twenty in gematria is Kesser,
according to the explanation in Likkutei Torah there on the verse,
"Lift up the head... by their skulls, from twenty years old...,"
for "their skulls" is Kesser
(Galgaltha),
and by drawing down the encompassing lights of Abba, it is possible to elevate to Galgaltha,
Kesser.
That is to say,
that after twenty years, they can receive, in addition to the aspect of Chayah of the tzaddik's soul, also from the aspect of his Yechidah,
as explained in Likkutei Torah there, that the encompassing lights of Abba and Galgaltha are Chayah and Yechidah].
